title: Real Estate
tagline: Agents, brokers, property managers, and appraisers — the business of property.
summary: Real estate careers run on licensure, local knowledge, and relationships: residential and commercial sales, property management, and appraisal. This roadmap covers getting licensed, building a book of clients, transactions end-to-end, and the broker/ownership ladder.

sources.label: BLS OOH — Real Estate Brokers and Sales Agents

detail.description: Real estate careers center on transactions: agents represent buyers and sellers, brokers run offices, property managers operate rentals, and appraisers value property — all licensed at the state level.
detail.why: Property is most families' largest asset, so demand persists in every market — and commission-based income rewards hustle directly.
learn: Read the BLS OOH profile of brokers and sales agents
Compare residential sales, commercial, property management, and appraisal lanes
Shadow an agent for a day or attend an open house
Note your state's licensing authority and requirements

tasks: Rent, buy, or sell property for clients; perform duties such as study property listings, interview prospective clients, accompany clients to property sites, and discuss conditions of sale.

detail.description: The lanes differ in rhythm and pay: residential sales (fast, personal), commercial (larger deals, longer cycles), property management (recurring income), appraisal (analytical, fee-based).
detail.why: Your lane determines your license endorsements, daily schedule, and income model — choosing deliberately shapes everything after.

detail.description: Agents read their market daily: inventory, days-on-market, price-per-square-foot trends, interest-rate effects, and neighborhood-level comparables.
